newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian RBA subdidiary plans to buy local bank.
newsitem.headline: Croatian RBA subdidiary plans to buy local bank.

text.p: The Croatian subsidiary of Raiffeisenbank Austria (RBA) plans to buy a smaller Croatian bank in a bid to expand its operations, president Zdenko Adrovic was quoted as saying by business magazine Banka.
Adrovic said in an interview opening new outlets in coastal towns of Rijeka and Split were among the bank's strategic priorities in the next three years.
"In addition we are considering a merger with a smaller private bank, which has an adequate retail network, to expand our business and client structure," he said.
No one at RBA, the first foreign bank to open in Croatia, was available for comment.
Adrovic was appointed at the helm of its management board after a former head and another member resigned amid a policy dispute in September.
He said increasing competition in Croatia's overcrowded banking sector under pressure by large local and foreign banks would probably force smaller banks to merge in order to survive.
To avoid being pushed aside, RBA aimed to boost its total assets to 400-450 million German marks within the next three years.
As a first step the bank doubled its capital to 30 million marks in May.
